pages.title: What is a structure used for
pages.content:
## What is a structure used for

C programs execute from `main`. This page introduces **Structures in C** and the syntax and runtime behaviour needed to use the concept correctly.

callout.title: Key Concept
callout.text: Focus on the C language rule illustrated by What is a structure used for.

codeCard.code:
#include <stdio.h>
struct Student{char name[20];int mark;};int main(void){struct Student s={"Asha",92};printf("%s %d\n",s.name,s.mark);return 0;}

checkpoint.question: Which statement is correct about Structures in C in C?
options: It follows the C language rules and the specified input/output contract for Structures in C.
It can ignore declared data types and input format.
It should depend on undefined compiler behaviour.
It must use global variables for every value.
checkpoint.explanation: The first option correctly describes how Structures in C should be applied in C.
